analysis.title: Biopharma: More 340B Scrubbing Likely To Come; Policy Changes Unlikely to Have NT Impact
key_insights: RBC spoke with a 340B drug pricing expert, a former Bristol Myers Squibb 340B strategy lead. The expert expects manufacturers to keep investing in data tools to remove duplicate discounts, which RBC thinks will support continued favorable gross-to-net (GTN) benefits.
RBC takes away that the seemingly outsized 3Q26 benefit from 340B scrubbing may be a trend rather than a one-time item. That could support the sustainability of large biopharma revenue trajectories.
The growing role of 340B is making the channel mix more heavily discounted overall, particularly for oncology, immunology and physician-administered drugs.
RBC expects the impact of the HRSA 340B rebate pilot to be limited in 2027.
The most recent HRSA estimate puts the 340B program at $100B at the discounted price, equal to $240B at wholesale acquisition cost (WAC). That outsizes Medicaid and competes with Medicare.

The expert estimates 340B accounts for 30-40% of volume for physician-administered drugs, versus about 5% for commonly used pharmacy drugs. The impact varies by drug and by prescriber base, so it is hard to quantify precisely.

Drugs are often discounted through channels like Medicaid and then rebated again under 340B, because 340B status is often unknown at the time of billing. The expert says manufacturers have always tried to remove these duplicate discounts and that no single new trend caused the 3Q jump.

More discount types (IRA, Medicare inflation rebates, discretionary rebates) and the growing program size raise the incentive to address duplicate discounts. The program has grown about 20% y/y for the past 6 years, and the expert expects scrubbing to continue.

Large, well-resourced manufacturers are likely recouping about 65-75% of identified duplicate-discount claims and may have some room to improve. Smaller manufacturers are likely recovering only about 30%.

The expert sees a ceiling well short of 100% recovery without policy change. Barriers include PBM contract provisions capping disputes and the need for a third-party auditor to challenge covered entities.

The SECURE (House) and SUSTAIN (Senate) proposals are meant to replace the HRSA Rebate Model due to start in January 2027. The expert sees them as lacking power to enforce data submission by covered entities and unlikely to have real impact for several years. Manufacturers will still face 340B as they enter MFP (Medicare negotiated price) pricing.
Oncology and immunology have the highest 340B exposure, followed by categories such as mental health. Continued investment in data could leave room to improve gross-to-net from current levels.
CAR-T therapies currently have relatively low 340B exposure, but that could rise as they move into the outpatient setting.

The HRSA pilot is expected to launch January 1, 2027 with 21 IRA-selected drugs from the 2026 and 2027 cohorts. Manufacturers would honor 340B pricing as a rebate and receive the required data upfront. The expert called the pilot 'too narrow' to quantify and expects a muted impact, since manufacturers will keep their own data collection for other channels.

sector_views.rationale: RBC sees continued gross-to-net benefits from 340B duplicate-discount scrubbing, offset by a more heavily discounted channel mix, especially in oncology, immunology and physician-administered drugs. Proposed policy changes are unlikely to matter near term.

earnings_insights: RBC says large biopharmas appeared to benefit disproportionately from 340B scrubbing practices in their 3Q26 earnings. The report gives no company names or figures.
risk_factors: The 340B program keeps growing about 20% y/y, which pushes channel mix toward heavier discounts.
Recovery of duplicate discounts is capped by PBM contract provisions and third-party auditor requirements.
Legislative turnover could change how 340B policy is handled.
Oncology, immunology and physician-administered drugs carry the most 340B exposure.
CAR-T 340B exposure could rise as treatments move to the outpatient setting.

tension_points.bull_case: Manufacturers keep investing in data solutions to remove duplicate discounts. Large players recoup about 65-75% of claims and may have more room, which RBC thinks supports favorable gross-to-net and large biopharma revenue trajectories.
tension_points.bear_case: Recovery is capped well short of 100% by PBM contract limits and third-party auditor requirements. Meanwhile 340B growth of about 20% y/y makes the channel mix more heavily discounted, especially in oncology, immunology and physician-administered drugs.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Legislation that enforces data submission by covered entities would raise the ceiling, while a rebate model that does not address duplicate discounts in other channels leaves the cap in place.

theme_stances.key_argument: Continued investment in data solutions to combat duplicate discounts should contribute to continued favorable gross-to-net benefits.
theme_stances.evidence: will likely contribute to continued favorable GTN benefits
